items.s: American scientists ____ to find out which activities made days better.

tfn.s: The study proves that meeting friends makes people happier.
tfn.why: The text says: "The study cannot prove that following its pattern will make everybody happy."

tfn.s: The researchers used information from two large surveys.
tfn.why: The text says the researchers studied two large American surveys, one from 2013 and another from 2021.

tfn.s: A technology company paid for the research.
tfn.why: The text does not say who paid for the research.

tfn.s: After about two hours of socialising, extra time made little difference.
tfn.why: The text says extra time "did not seem to make a big difference" after about two hours.

tfn.s: Very long working hours were linked with higher happiness.
tfn.why: The text says very long working hours "were linked with lower happiness".

focus.note: Some linking words show a result (so), some show a contrast (however, while), and some set a condition (unless). Decide what the sentence needs.

items.s: More than 15,000 participants ____ how they had spent a day.

tfn.s: The researchers hoped to find a magic routine that would work for everyone.
tfn.why: The text says their aim "was not to discover a magic routine".

tfn.s: The benefit of socialising kept growing the longer people spent with others.
tfn.why: The text says the benefit "appeared to level off after roughly two hours".

tfn.s: All three Guardian writers felt happier after following the suggested patterns.
tfn.why: The text only says the experiment was a reminder that timetables are hard to follow.

tfn.s: Working up to six hours was not clearly linked to a poorer day.
tfn.why: The text says "up to six hours was not clearly linked to a poorer day".

tfn.s: The writer suggests that people who can stop work after six hours may be better off than people on a long shift.
tfn.why: The text says such a person "may also have more money, flexibility or support".

focus.note: Check the grammar after the gap. Despite needs an -ing form or a noun, while otherwise, whereas and provided can join clauses or sentences in different ways.

items.s: ____ feeling tired, she went to meet her friends after work.

items.s: Critics questioned the ____ of data collected from self-reported diaries.
Her sudden ____ from public life surprised her colleagues.
His ____ attitude to leisure meant that even holidays were planned by the minute.
The researchers were careful not to overstate the ____ of their findings.

tfn.s: The study shows that meeting friends causes a better day.
tfn.why: The text says it relied on associations, not experiments showing cause and effect.

tfn.s: According to the study, a seven-hour working day is more likely to go with a worse day than a five-hour one.
tfn.why: Up to six hours did not clearly undermine a good day, but "longer stretches were associated with a sharper decline".

tfn.s: The Guardian writers reported feeling happier after following their routines.
tfn.why: The text only says their attempts highlighted the obstacle of real-life limits.

tfn.s: The writer advises readers to ignore the evidence from the study.
tfn.why: The text says the sensible conclusion is "neither to worship a formula nor ignore the evidence".

tfn.s: The findings on socialising and on work each describe a point beyond which the pattern changes.
tfn.why: Socialising levels off after around two hours, and work is linked to a sharper decline after six.

focus.note: These are formal linkers. Albeit and notwithstanding sit in the middle of a clause, hence and lest have strict patterns, and conversely turns an idea round.

speak.title: Role-play: planning a free Saturday
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You both have a free Saturday. You want to spend the whole day together with a big group of friends. Suggest a plan and explain why it would be a good day.

b.text: You've had a very busy week and you need some time alone. Say what you'd like to do instead and try to agree on a plan that suits you both.

phrases: I was thinking we could meet everyone for lunch.
That's a nice idea, but I'm really tired this week.
How about a short walk, just the two of us?
I'd rather spend the afternoon on my own.
We could do both if we keep it short.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what plan did you agree on, and who gave up more?
